findings.title: Call to non-existent no-argument isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not compile
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate() calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only method added to its superclass UsernamePasswordForm is isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) at UsernamePasswordForm.java:160. There is no no-argument overload in UsernamePasswordForm, AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator, or the shown superclass chain, so this file fails compilation and the whole services module cannot build. The call should pass the relevant user, e.g. isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), or a no-argument overload must be defined.

findings.title: Conditional passkeys are now only filled when a user is already known, breaking initial ID-less passkey login
findings.body: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) requires user != null, and authenticate() (line 115) and challenge(context,error,field) (line 137) now use it instead of the previous logic that filled WebAuthn data when no user was selected yet. On a first login through UsernamePasswordForm/UsernameForm no user is set, so WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.fillContextForm() is never called, ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI/challenge/RP data are not put on the login page, and discoverable (ID-less) passkeys cannot auto-login or be offered. The same applies after a failed password attempt in a normal login where the user is cleared. The helper must also return true for the not-yet-identified case (user == null) in addition to the re-authentication case.

findings.title: Re-authentication passkey check does not verify the known user actually has a passkey credential
findings.body: For a known user, isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() only checks that the realm/feature passkeys flag is on; it never checks user.credentialManager().isConfiguredFor(webauthnAuth.getCredentialType()). Because WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() now always returns false, fillContextForm() also no longer bails out when the user has no WebAuthn authenticators. Consequently every re-authenticating user in a passkeys-enabled realm, including password-only users, loses the UsernameForm skip-success shortcut (UsernameForm.java:47) and is presented with passkey conditional-UI/authenticate UI they cannot use, instead of going straight to password/broker re-authentication.

findings.title: reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey test disables passkeys realm-wide instead of testing a user without a passkey
findings.body: The test named reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey sets WebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled to FALSE for the whole realm, so the absence of the webauth form only proves the realm flag is honoured. It does not cover the distinct and currently broken case of a passkeys-enabled realm with a user (test-user@localhost, who only has a password) who has no passwordless credential, which is the case a credential check in isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() needs to handle. Add/adjust the test to keep passkeys enabled in the realm while the re-authenticating user has no passkey and assert no passkey UI is shown and password re-authentication still works.
